milestone.title: raul TUI lane-load latency: parallel subprocess + per-lane TTL cache

intent.outcome: Switching lanes in raul's TUI feels instant — Overview, Milestones, Path, Backlog, and Board all render the new lane's data with no perceptible shell-out delay on a warm plan. A user toggling rapidly with h/l lands on each lane's data within one frame because the second-through-Nth lane visits hit a TTL cache. On cold cache, the Board and Overview lanes (the heaviest) use parallel subprocess fan-out instead of serial calls.

problem.description: Every lane navigation in raul spawns fresh mp subprocess calls (crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs::load_data_for_lane → load_dashboard | load_milestones | load_path_data | load_backlog | load_board). Profiling on a real plan shows: mp status ≈ 500ms (runs path_engine::build_lanes, inbox::build_inbox, reviews::pending_review_count, validate_plan, load_annotations — all of which load the plan); mp list milestones --with-findings ≈ 155ms cold / 6ms warm; mp reviews lifecycle ≈ 38ms; mp list milestones ≈ 38ms; mp path lanes ≈ 38ms. Overview lane pays 500ms (status) + 7ms (inbox) ≈ 510ms serial; Board lane pays 155ms + 38ms ≈ 190ms cold. The two subprocess calls in load_board run sequentially when they could fan out. There is no per-lane cache, so a user hammering h/l to peek at lanes pays the full load cost on every visit. The load happens on the TUI's blocking event-loop path, so the user sees a visible stall with no spinner / no feedback. M134 (smoothness) addresses render-side perf but is orthogonal to data loading. The cheapest fix is to (a) parallelize the multi-call loads and (b) add a short-TTL per-lane cache so rapid back-and-forth is instant.

in_scope: Parallel subprocess fan-out in load_board: mp list milestones --with-findings and mp reviews lifecycle run concurrently via std::thread::spawn (each thread does its MpRunner::run and sends the parsed Value back through a channel), parsed on the main thread. Eliminates ~38ms serial overhead on every Board visit.
Parallel subprocess fan-out in load_dashboard: mp status and mp inbox run concurrently. Eliminates the ~7ms inbox serialization on every Overview visit (smaller win, but consistent pattern).

Per-lane TTL cache (LaneCache in crates/raul/src/tui/lane_cache.rs): keyed by (Lane, plan_dir_mtime_secs) so a plan-file write invalidates automatically; values are the loaded Vec<...> / DashboardSnapshot / Value payloads; default TTL 2000ms, configurable via RAUL_LANE_CACHE_TTL_MS. Lookup returns Some(payload) when fresh, None otherwise.
load_data_for_lane consults the cache first; on miss, runs the load, stores the result, returns it. Cache writes are fail-silent: a failing load returns Err and does not poison the cache.

Cache invalidation hook: lane_cache.invalidate(lane) called from every successful mutation path in runner.rs — create_approval_annotation, resolve_annotation, reopen_annotation, approve/block/unblock/request-grooming, plus any other runner.rs::run_raw success. Tests pin that a mutation followed by a lane-switch fetches fresh data.

Tests in crates/raul/tests/tui_load_cache.rs: parallel join produces both values within the longer-of-the-two latency (not the sum); cache returns the same payload within TTL; cache invalidates on plan-file mtime change; mutation calls invalidate the affected lane.
Manual verification: time a 10x h/l toggle cycle before and after; expect ≤20% of the cold time on warm-cache hits.
out_of_scope: Long-lived mp daemon / Unix-socket IPC — separate follow-up milestone. Eliminates Rust process startup cost (the 6ms baseline) but is a real piece of work; defer until we know whether the cache + parallel wins are sufficient.
Inlining path_engine::build_lanes into raul — would skip the mp status shell-out entirely but couples the two crates and bloats raul's binary. Defer.
Skipping validate_plan on mp status — a separate optimization on the mp side; track as a tweak if perf still bites after this milestone.
Render-side perf — M134 (smoothness), M135 (ViewState) cover it.
Per-call memoization at the MpRunner layer — would also help CLI tools (raul status, raul backlog), but those are out of TUI scope; revisit if it shows up in dogfood.

design_decisions.choice: std::thread::spawn + std::sync::mpsc channel instead of tokio
design_decisions.rationale: raul's TUI is synchronous on crossterm; introducing tokio would be a much larger architectural change (M138 already touches dispatch). std::thread is the lightest tool that fits. We only have 2 concurrent calls in flight per lane-load, so a single channel pair per load is fine.

mtime is cheap (one stat call) and correct for the failure mode we care about — external writes (the agent editing a milestone, an mp command from another tool) invalidate the cache. A content hash would be slower and unnecessary; mtime is what M113's advisory lock already uses for write detection.

design_decisions.choice: TTL = 2000ms default, configurable via RAUL_LANE_CACHE_TTL_MS env var
design_decisions.rationale: Long enough that h/l mashing doesn't re-fetch (one frame is ~16ms, so 2s covers ~125 lane switches); short enough that a user pausing to read sees fresh data when they come back. Configurable so we can tune from dogfood without recompiling.

design_decisions.choice: Cache lives in the TUI runner, not the MpRunner
design_decisions.rationale: MpRunner is a thin shell-out wrapper; adding caching there would also affect non-TUI callers (raul status, raul backlog CLI), which we don't want to surprise. Keeping the cache at the TUI boundary matches the scope and avoids changing public raul CLI behavior.

steps.action: Add a parallel_pair helper (in MpRunner or in a small raul::tui::io module) that runs two closure-based MpRunner calls concurrently via std::thread::spawn + std::sync::mpsc, and returns both results. Wire it into load_board (mp list milestones --with-findings + mp reviews lifecycle) so the total wall-clock is max(t1,t2)+overhead.
steps.done_when: load_board returns within max(t1,t2)+overhead instead of t1+t2 serial; tui_load_cache.rs::parallel_board_returns_within_max_latency passes.

steps.action: Apply parallel_pair to load_dashboard (mp status + mp inbox). Same pattern as S1.

Wire LaneCache into load_data_for_lane in runner.rs: consult cache first; on miss, run load, store result, return; on hit, return cached Value. Add invalidate() calls into successful mutation paths: create_approval_annotation, resolve_annotation, reopen_annotation, approve/block/unblock/request-grooming. Failures do not invalidate.
steps.done_when: Rapid h/l toggle within TTL hits cache; mutation followed by same-lane re-entry fetches fresh data; failing mutation does not invalidate.

steps.action: Create crates/raul/src/tui/lane_cache.rs with a LaneCache struct. Fields: per-Lane entry (Option<(Instant, serde_json::Value)>), plan_dir_mtime_secs (i64), ttl (Duration default 2s, override via RAUL_LANE_CACHE_TTL_MS env). Methods: get(lane) -> Option<Value>, put(lane, value), invalidate(lane), invalidate_all(), plan_dir_mtime(path). Cache key implicitly is (Lane, stored plan_dir_mtime_secs); a mtime change on the plan dir triggers invalidate_all on the next get.
steps.done_when: LaneCache compiles; unit tests for get/put/invalidate/is_fresh pass; mtime bump triggers invalidate_all.

findings.description: M143 H1/H2 review: mtime wiring was startup-only; plan-dir lookup hardcoded master-plan/. + cwd fallback. Remediation: exposed MpRunner::mp_dir() and project_root(), added LaneCache::check_and_update_mtime, wired into load_data_for_lane. Re-review H1+H2.

findings.description: Code review (remediation applied): parallel_pair rewrote to use std::thread::scope (Rust 1.63+ stable, edition 2021) instead of raw pointer casts + unsafe to satisfy 'static on thread closures. The new shape drops the unsafe block, removes the JoinHandle recovery helper (scope auto-joins and panics propagate to the existing catch_unwind in tui::runner), and keeps the same fan-out semantics. LaneCache: removed unused Clone + Default derives (Clone would deep-copy the HashMap + arc-clone each Value; Default is built explicitly via with_default_ttl). Humanize test tightened: removed unreachable 'ends_with(s ago)' and '0m ago' assertions; added a positive '5m ago' test for the < 1h bucket.
findings.author: external-review-agent
findings.summary: M143 review: replace unsafe parallel_pair with thread::scope + tighten humanize test (3 fixes)

findings.description: invalidate_after_lifecycle_write clears Milestones+Overview only — never Board. Approve/block/unblock leave Board cached. plan_mtime_secs is second granularity; same-second rewrite does not bump mtime. Stale Board possible for up to TTL (~2s). Also invalidate Lane::Board (and Backlog if needed). Location: runner_helpers.rs:491-493
